title: Glad for you
hookLine: the third: joy in others' joy

cards: The group chat lights up. A friend got the job: the one you both applied for, maybe, or one you didn't know you wanted until they got it. Thumbs pile up.
Someone sends confetti. One thumb hovers a second longer than the rest. Sorrow for a friend in trouble can come easily.
Gladness for a friend who just pulled ahead is a different muscle. Buddhist teachers give it its own name, and its own place among the four boundless states.

teach.b: After loving-kindness and compassion comes mudita: gladness at another's good fortune. Compassion meets someone in their worst moment.
Mudita meets them in their best one, and that can be harder, because their best moment doesn't need us.

Buddhaghosa, in his Path of Purification, describes mudita as a gladness that comes from seeing others do well, and he says its work is not envying. Envy keeps a ledger: their win is my loss. Mudita throws the ledger out.
Their win is simply a win, and there's more joy in the world than there was this morning. Like compassion, gladness has a near enemy that can pass for it.
Buddhaghosa names a worldly, excited glee, the kind that's really about getting things, not about the other person. Real mudita is quieter: glad for them, even if nothing in it is for us.
Buddhaghosa doesn't begin with a rival. He suggests a cheerful companion, a friend whose good news is easy to love.
Let the gladness grow there, then try it on someone neutral, and someday on the friend who got the job you wanted.

how: In Buddhist meditation on the four boundless states, practitioners cultivate mudita by recalling a friend's good fortune and rejoicing in it, then widening that gladness to others.

o: pride in your own hard-won success
gladness at someone else's good fortune

games.q: the four boundless states so far — tap the pairs.
p: the second: wishing suffering to lift
the third: glad at another's good
what mudita's job is to undo

s: mudita's near enemy is a worldly, excited glee
Buddhaghosa names a glee about getting things, which can pass for gladness.
Buddhaghosa says start mudita practice with a rival
Buddhaghosa suggests beginning with a cheerful companion whose good news is easy to love.

games.q: a friend just got the job you both wanted. mudita asks what?
o: say congratulations and change the subject fast.
let yourself be glad that it happened to them.
games.why: mudita is gladness at another's good fortune; its job, Buddhaghosa says, is not envying.

practice: Bring to mind one piece of someone else's good news, a new baby, a recovery, a promotion, a small win mentioned in passing, and picture their face as they told it.
Let yourself be glad, for no reason except that it happened to them, and if something tight shows up, a little comparing, notice it kindly and come back to their face.

wordCard.voice: Mudita. Gladness at another person's good fortune, the third of the four boundless states. Today's word.

orig.note: Pali and Sanskrit: gladness at others' good fortune, the third boundless state.

carryVoice: Your line: more joy in the world. It's a different muscle, and it grows. Day eight hundred forty-eight, and counting.
